Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics, CDs_and_Vinyl, macro-average validation
HR@10. Start from RecHarness sasrec_perdataset. Preprocessing seed=0 and training

test metrics are unavailable during search. Retain all four categories and dataset
routing. DATA_DIR must remain os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; write artifacts beneath
your trial directory, as the baseline does. Training may change model architecture,
loss, optimizer, sampling and hyperparameters, as in RecHarness. Do not alter input
splits, invent metrics, read hidden test files, fetch extra datasets/pretrained weights,
or change the host evaluator. Changes to inference must also update the predictor
writer so working/predict.py loads the trained architecture. Keep execution single-GPU;
the host provides four concurrent trial slots and 64 CPU cores. No shell actions,
filesystem inspection, or training tools are needed in the LLM call: return code.
All training, diagnostics, debugging and failed trials consume the method's shared
43,200 GPU-second search budget. LLM time and final held-out inference are recorded
separately, matching run2.sh's separate final-evaluation step.

standalone default of 300); this same environment default applies here.

METHOD: self_evolverec

Diagnostic task adapter: diagnosis_tools.py must retain class DiagnosisProbe(view, device)
and method run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning metrics and metric_definitions.
view.model is the actual trained nn.Module. view.item_emb, log2feats(sequence),
predict_score(features, items), user_train, meta_data, review_data implement the
initial SASRec compatibility contract. Adapt probes when changing the architecture.
train_loader yields (None, sequence, positive, negative), tensors of shape B x L.

Review ratings/text, item ratings/categories/prices/stores are NOT available in this
shared RecHarness task. Never invent them. Simulator diversity/conformity traits are
explicitly unobserved. Twenty real training users (five/category) receive full-catalog
unseen-item recommendations, as the native simulator requires. Selection uses the
common macro validation HR@10, replacing the native HR@5/NDCG@5 combined score.

NATIVE ROLE: Reflection Agent

You are an expert research assistant. You will receive a research report (in Markdown) and a newly proposed idea for that report's research problem. Your job is to identify any gaps or issues—such as missing details, logical flaws, or questionable evaluations of novelty, impact, or implementation difficulty.  

- If the report and idea contain all necessary information, do not generate any follow-up questions.  
- If you detect a knowledge gap or something that needs deeper exploration, generate one or more self-contained follow-up queries. Each query must include enough context so that a web search could answer it, For each query, give a short note explaining why you use the query and what you hope it will reveal.
- Focus on technical details, implementation specifics, and any emerging methods or references that were overlooked.  
- Use clear, direct language and avoid unnecessary jargon.

 ## Search results
Recent work supports testing richer negatives before increasing SASRec complexity. [SCE (RecSys 2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.18721) approximates full cross-entropy using GPU-efficient maximum-inner-product search to concentrate computation on informative logits, reporting substantial memory savings while preserving ranking quality. [eSASRec (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.06450) identifies sampled softmax plus improved Transformer layers as a strong combination, although its gains do not isolate the loss alone. [gSASRec’s 2025 extended study](https://eprints.gla.ac.uk/336442/2/336442.pdf) shows that negative count and BCE overconfidence both matter; generalized BCE offers an alternative to switching objectives. The [RecSys 2025 LogQ implementation](https://github.com/NonameUntitled/logq/) also provides SASRec comparisons of uniform, in-batch and mixed sampling with sampling-probability correction.

Hardness needs safeguards. [CATS (SIGIR 2026)](https://iris.uniroma1.it/handle/11573/1775773) uses item clusters and adaptive sampling to balance informative negatives against likely false negatives. [EMM (2026)](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0893608026004090), in broader contrastive recommendation, combines refreshed memory candidates, hard–random mixtures, ID exclusion and similarity-window filtering. Practical inference for this task: compare uniform multi-negative softmax or generalized BCE against a modest hard–random mixture; mask duplicate targets and known training positives, and treat similarity filtering as an ablation because similarity does not establish relevance. LogQ corrects sampling bias, not false-negative labels. These sources provide no evidence of improvement on the pinned Electronics task. Lower loss or larger margins remain diagnostics; select using the unchanged four-category macro validation HR@10, report Electronics separately, and compare trials at matched GPU cost.

---

Recent work supports modeling complementarity separately from semantic similarity. [Revisiting Graph Projections (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.09209) infers complementary recommendations using a directed, weighted item graph projected from historical user–item interactions, offering a simple interaction-only starting point without pretrained language weights. [SComGNN (AAAI 2024)](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/28734) models complementary products through both relevance and dissimilarity: low-pass and mid-pass graph filters capture these components, with attention combining them. These results motivate retaining directional transition evidence rather than relying entirely on embedding similarity; neither establishes that arbitrary consecutive purchases are true complements.

For the constrained benchmark, a reasonable synthesis—not a verified published recipe—is a SASRec residual combining smoothed directed transition scores with separate source/target item embeddings and a title/description encoder trained from scratch using token embeddings plus pooling or a small CNN. Text can share statistical strength across sparse items, while asymmetric interaction scores learn which related items tend to follow others. Compare transition-only, text-only, and combined variants using macro validation HR@10 across all four categories. Treat graph edges as predictive associations, not compatibility labels; semantic similarity does not establish substitution, and purchase order does not prove a satisfied need. The search did not identify a verified 2024–2026 method satisfying every restriction simultaneously. [STAR (CIKM 2024)](https://pure.uva.nl/ws/files/245900224/3627673.3679999.pdf) is relevant text-recommendation work, but its transformer-based representations and review inputs make it unsuitable as a direct match.

---

Recent work supports testing separate representations of immediate intent and enduring preferences, but does not establish that a single SASRec representation necessarily conflates them. [HLSDMRec (2025)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ipm.2025.104425) combines a local LSTM for short-term transitions, denoised Mamba for long-term preferences, and adaptive fusion. [C-TLSAN (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.13021) incorporates item descriptions into long- and short-term attention, reporting improvements across ten Amazon categories. [GLSRec (2026)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.datak.2026.102606) additionally models transitions across users’ sequences, addressing the limited transition evidence within sparse individual histories. These results motivate architectural ablations; their reported gains cannot be transferred directly to the pinned RecHarness evaluation.

A practical hypothesis for this benchmark: retain SASRec, add a recent-window intent branch and a pooled historical-preference branch, then learn a small gate conditioned on history length, representation agreement, and observed interaction gaps. Compare against fixed fusion and each branch alone. For temporal modeling, foundational [TiSASRec](https://jiachengli1995.github.io/files/wsdm20.pdf) combines absolute positions with relative time intervals and evaluates Amazon CDs/Vinyl, among other datasets. Test a lightweight bucketed time-gap attention bias before adopting a larger encoder. Recurrent interests could be represented through similarity to previously observed items, while recommendations still exclude seen items. These are proposed adaptations, not demonstrated benchmark improvements.
